newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador president rules out convertibility plan.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador president rules out convertibility plan.

text.p: Ecuador's new president, Fabian Alarcon, ruled out Friday the introduction of a convertibility plan that would have pegged the value of the local sucre currency to the dollar.

"When one refers to convertibility, for the moment it is absolutely ruled out. The economic and social conditions to apply such a system in Ecuador are not there," Alarcon told foreign correspondents.

The government of President Abdala Bucaram, ousted by Ecuador's Congress last week, had planned to launch a convertibility system similar to one in place in Argentina. The sucre was to have been pegged at a rate of four sucres to the dollar from July this year.
But, Alarcon, chosen by Congress to serve as interim president until elections are held next year, said a new currency system was not on the cards.

"Convertibility needs a degree of economic stability, a reactivation of the productive system and certain economic parameters, degrees of credibility and confidence that definitely do not adequately exist in Ecuador," he said.
The new president said some of his government's main aims will be to attack the fiscal deficit, reduce public spending and work on a new tax policy.
He admitted the administration could not introduce medium or long term policies because of the short time it will have in office. A new government will take over after elections.
Alarcon also said he intended to visit the United States in coming months after an official invitation from the U.S. administration.
